items.question: Why is the supreme means praised as the supreme word of the great lord?
premises: The verse opens with then.
It names the supreme means.
It identifies the supreme word of the great lord.
items.inference: The opening presents the supreme means as the supreme word of the great lord.
uncertainties: paraupayikaṃ may be read as supreme means or means of the supreme.
items.plain_english: Then the supreme means of the great lord is praised, the supreme word indeed.

items.question: What extra element is distinguished in the supreme greatness previously declared as mere light?
premises: The verse recalls what was declared as mere light.
It calls that greatness supreme and Bhairava-related.
It says only freedom is extra there.
items.inference: The supreme greatness is mere light, with freedom as the only additional element distinguished.
uncertainties: svatantratāmātramadhikaṃ may mean freedom alone is additional.
items.plain_english: What was declared as mere light, the supreme Bhairava greatness, has only freedom distinguished there.

items.question: How does the light give light-ness to all without anything existing apart from it?
premises: The light gives light-ness to all.
Nothing exists apart from that light.
The universe appears as being.
items.inference: All light-ness comes from one light, and the universe appears within it without separation.
uncertainties: sadvāvabhāsate may mean appears as real or appears as existent.
items.plain_english: That light gives light-ness to all; nothing exists apart from it, and the universe appears as being.

items.question: Why is the supreme lord called the revealer of the spectacle of creation and destruction?
premises: The supreme lord is unbarred in own self-space.
He reveals the spectacle of creation and destruction.
The spectacle is of this much.
items.inference: The unbarred supreme lord reveals the whole spectacle of creation and destruction.
uncertainties: iyataḥ may qualify the spectacle or the lord.
items.plain_english: Therefore that supreme lord, unbarred in his own self-space, reveals the spectacle of creation and destruction.

items.question: How do world activities appear unmixed in one conscious lord like earth and water in a pure mirror?
premises: Earth, water, and so forth shine in a pure mirror.
They remain unmixed there.
World activities likewise appear in one conscious lord.
items.inference: World activities appear distinctly and unmixed in one conscious lord, like reflections in a pure mirror.
uncertainties: amiśrāḥ may modify reflections or activities.
items.plain_english: As earth, water, and so forth shine unmixed in a pure mirror, so world activities appear in one conscious lord.

items.question: Why does only form appear in pure form when similar shining occurs in eye, mirror, sky, and water?
premises: Similar shining occurs in eye, mirror, sky, and water.
In pure form, form alone appears.
The verse emphasizes this with indeed.
items.inference: Pure form reveals form alone, unlike mixed media where similar shining occurs.
uncertainties: sadṛśaṃ may modify shining or form.
items.plain_english: Similar shining appears in eye, mirror, sky, and water; indeed, in pure form only form appears.

items.question: Why is the hidden passionate woman not satisfied by touching the mirror reflecting her beloved?
premises: The woman touches the mirror with her breast-pots.
The mirror reflects the beloved beautifully.
She is not satisfied.
items.inference: Touching a reflected beloved in a mirror does not satisfy desire.
items.plain_english: Though the hidden passionate woman touches with her breast-pots the mirror reflecting her beloved beautifully, she is not satisfied.

items.question: Why is touch not pure while form alone is pure in this mirror example?
premises: Touch of it is not pure.
Form alone is so.
Purity is extreme dense union of same kind.
items.inference: Touch lacks purity because purity requires extreme dense union of same kind, which form alone has.
items.plain_english: Indeed touch of it is not pure; form alone is so, because purity is extreme dense union of same kind.

items.question: What is purity according to the guru for one who does not abandon self-light?
premises: Purity is seeing capacity of the different from non-difference in self.
It belongs to one who does not abandon self-light.
The guru taught this.
items.inference: Purity is the capacity to see difference without losing non-difference in self-light.
items.plain_english: Purity, as the guru taught, is the seeing capacity of the different arising from non-difference in self, for one who does not abandon self-light.

items.question: Why is purity primary only for the one consciousness-lord, while other purity is partial and by his will?
premises: Purity is primary for one consciousness-lord.
Other purity is partial from all sides.
Such other purity occurs by his will.
items.inference: Only the consciousness-lord has primary purity; all other purity is partial and dependent on his will.
uncertainties: aṃśāṃśikātaḥ may mean partiality of parts.
items.plain_english: Purity is primary for the one consciousness-lord; elsewhere it is partial, by his will.

items.question: What is obstructive for beings and what is non-obstructive true knowledge?
premises: The obstructive thing for beings is body-maya-natured.
That belongs to them only.
True-knowledge-natured is non-obstructive.
items.inference: Maya-bodied obstruction belongs to beings, while true knowledge is non-obstructive.
uncertainties: bhāvānāṃ may mean beings or states.
items.plain_english: For beings, the obstructive body-maya nature belongs to them only; true-knowledge nature is non-obstructive.

items.question: How does the boon-giver shine by revealing an appearance of both forms everywhere?
premises: The boon-giver reveals an appearance of both forms.
He shines everywhere by image and reflection view.
Thus both forms appear.
items.inference: The boon-giver shines everywhere by revealing an appearance that has both forms, seen as image and reflection.
uncertainties: ubhayākāram may mean both forms or both aspects.
items.plain_english: Thus revealing an appearance of both forms, the boon-giver shines everywhere by image and reflection view.
